ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a polygon with 18 vertices, and each vertex is marked with a small circle. Vertex A is at the very top; the number 20 is marked beside a vertex at the lower left; the number 18 is marked beside a vertex at the lower right. Counting along the polygon from the figure, from A clockwise to the vertex where 18 is located, there are 7 edges between them; from A counterclockwise to the vertex where 20 is located, there are also 7 edges between them. Then reason: Let the vertex values clockwise starting from A be x_0, x_1, x_2, ..., where x_0=a, x_1=b. The problem says that the number at each vertex equals the sum of the numbers at the two adjacent vertices, so x_i=x_{i-1}+x_{i+1}, equivalently x_{i+1}=x_i-x_{i-1}. Recursing from this: x_0=a, x_1=b, x_2=b-a, x_3=-a, x_4=-b, x_5=a-b, x_6=a, and after that it cycles every 6. The 18-gon is exactly 3 periods. The vertex where 18 is located is 7 steps clockwise from A, namely x_7. Since the period is 6, x_7=x_1=b, so b=18. The vertex where 20 is located is 7 steps counterclockwise from A, namely x_{-7}, which corresponds by the period to x_5=a-b, so a-b=20. Substituting b=18 gives a-18=20, therefore a=38. The number at A is 38.
